title: Vehicle Art Director
verdict: A charming, readable low-poly go-kart with good proportions and a cheerful orange livery, but several areas (the driver figure, the cockpit's empty seat, and some finicky detail parts) keep it from showcase polish.
strengths: Clean, instantly readable go-kart silhouette with correct wide-track wheels, low-slung frame, exposed sidepods and nose (10-kart-orbit-a, 05-chase-racing)
Cheerful, on-brief sunny color scheme: bright orange body, warm wood-tone steering column, blue seat and driver suit read as toy-like and friendly (07-chase-ghost)
Nicely detailed driver in the chase/ghost shots with a blue helmet and gripped blue steering wheel that sells the kart identity (07-chase-ghost)
Wheels and tires have appropriate chunky proportions with orange hub accents that tie into the body color (10-kart-orbit-a)

issues.problem: The cockpit view from the driver's seat is dominated by a flat black dashboard slab with three plain dark circles and a barely-visible wheel rim; the green trigger-indicator blobs look like placeholder UI pasted onto the dash rather than modeled gauges (02-cockpit-countdown, 03-cockpit-racing, 01-cockpit-idle)
issues.fix: Model a proper stylized dash: replace the flat circles with low-poly dials/bezels, give the steering wheel a visible rim and spokes in the cockpit view, and integrate the throttle/brake feedback as actual lit gauge elements rather than floating green ovals

issues.problem: The driver figure is inconsistent and reads poorly: in orbit (10-kart-orbit-a) the seat looks nearly empty with only a vague dark torso, while in chase (07-chase-ghost) a full helmeted driver appears, suggesting the body mesh is thin/missing from some angles
issues.fix: Ensure the driver mesh is a solid, consistent low-poly figure with torso, arms reaching the wheel, and legs visible from all angles; fill the seat so orbit views don't look vacant

issues.problem: The rear/underside detail parts (exhaust pipe, silver floor pan, rear bumper rails) look thin and slightly scattered, reading as loose sticks rather than cohesive structure in chase and finish shots (09-chase-finished, 05-chase-racing)
issues.fix: Thicken and group the rear bumper/exhaust/floor geometry into a tidier chamfered assembly so the back of the kart reads as deliberate rather than stray edges

issues.problem: The ghost kart appears to use the identical opaque material/colors as the player kart in the distance (07-chase-ghost shows a teal-tinted kart top-right), making player vs ghost distinction rely entirely on faint translucency
issues.fix: Give the ghost a clearly distinct translucent/tinted material (e.g. uniform ghostly cyan with fresnel edge glow) so it reads unmistakably as a replay rather than a second solid kart

issues.problem: The seat and body surfaces are flat matte with no edge highlights or material variation, making the orange body panels look slightly plasticky and undetailed for a hero vehicle (10-kart-orbit-a)
issues.fix: Add subtle beveled edges, a light decal/number plate on the sidepods, and a hint of specular/trim contrast to give the bodywork more toy-like richness

title: Environment & Visual Cohesion Artist
verdict: The environment establishes a clean and readable baseline, but flat lighting and primitive scenery assets hold back the intended sunny, toy-like charm.
strengths: High-contrast red and white curbs combined with solid barriers make track boundaries extremely readable.
Low-poly clouds and layered mountains establish a cheerful, stylized backdrop.
The baseline color palette of blue skies and green terrain is bright and welcoming, fitting the intended direction.

issues.problem: The environment lacks directional cast shadows from trees, walls, and structures (visible in 05, 06), resulting in a flat, unlit appearance that completely contradicts the 'sunny' theme.
issues.fix: Add a primary directional sun light with shadow mapping enabled so that static objects cast clear, stylized low-poly shadows onto the track and grass.

issues.problem: The grandstand (10-kart-orbit-a) appears as a primitive block-out of stacked, heavily saturated primary-colored cubes that lack structural logic and clash with the rest of the scenery.
issues.fix: Replace the cube stack with a cohesive low-poly grandstand model featuring defined seating rows, support structures, and a unified, slightly pastel color scheme.

issues.problem: The track surface contains bizarre, blocky dark gray rectangular patches (04-cockpit-corner, 05-chase-racing) and the surrounding grass is a completely featureless flat plane, making the world feel empty and reducing the sense of speed.
issues.fix: Correct the geometry or texture mapping on the road to remove the dark patches, add a subtle scrolling grain to the asphalt, and scatter low-poly props (rocks, bushes, flowers) across the grass to provide visual speed references.

issues.problem: The exact same tree model is stamped repeatedly across the landscape without any variation in size or rotation (06-chase-corner).
issues.fix: Randomize the scale (e.g., +/- 20%) and Y-axis rotation of the placed trees, and introduce at least one additional foliage variant to break up the repetition.

title: UX & HUD Usability Lead
verdict: A clear, functional racing HUD with good hierarchy, but the central start overlays and VR comfort/actionability issues keep it short of showcase polish.
strengths: Top-right race HUD is compact, consistently placed, and generally legible against the sky in racing shots 02-07.
Speed, lap, time, best, and delta have a sensible information hierarchy, with speed emphasized clearly in orange.
Idle instructions panel in 01 and 10 communicates both desktop and VR controls before play starts.
Start, lap transition, ghost availability, and race completion are all communicated with distinct overlays.
Finish panel in 08-09 has strong hierarchy, readable lap breakdown, and clearly calls out the new best lap.

issues.problem: The large centered READY/GO overlay blocks the driving line and persists into active driving, especially in 02-03 where it covers the road during launch.
issues.fix: Shrink the GO card, move it slightly above the horizon or make it non-card text only, and fade it out within roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds after control begins.

issues.problem: The main race HUD is high and far to the upper-right in cockpit view, which is readable on desktop but likely uncomfortable in seated VR because key info requires looking away from the road, as seen in 03-04.
issues.fix: Add a VR-friendly diegetic or world-locked dashboard near the steering wheel/low center for speed, lap, and time, with the upper HUD minimized or optional in VR.

issues.problem: Finish state restart guidance is desktop-biased: 08-09 say 'Press R or Restart' but no visible Restart button is present on the finish card and no VR restart action is explained.
issues.fix: Put a large Restart button directly on the finish panel and add a VR-specific prompt such as 'Pull trigger to restart' or support gaze/ray selection.

issues.problem: The instructions panel is useful but slightly dense and awkwardly formatted in 01 and 10, with small text, square separators, and unclear arrow-key phrasing such as 'A D / Left Right'.
issues.fix: Convert controls into a two-column icon list with keyboard keycaps and VR trigger/wheel icons, using larger spacing and clearer labels like 'A/D or ←/→: steer'.

issues.problem: The persistent 'Enter XR' browser-style button remains visible during racing and finish screens in 02-09, competing with the HUD near the top center.
issues.fix: Hide or collapse the Enter XR affordance once the race starts, or move it into a pause/menu state so the racing HUD has visual priority.

title: Gameplay & Game Feel Designer
verdict: Sunny Circuit delivers a complete and readable time-trial loop with a working ghost and dual cameras, but is held back by a visually monotonous track layout, near-zero sense of speed in cockpit view, absent impact/off-track feedback, and a delta timer that never activates during the race.
strengths: Full race loop is intact and polished: READY state with clear dual-mode controls, GO! countdown, per-lap split display (screenshot 07), and a detailed 'Race complete' results screen with NEW BEST callout and lap-by-lap breakdown (screenshots 08-09)
Ghost kart appears correctly on lap 2 in a distinct translucent blue colour, clearly differentiated from the player kart, giving the core time-trial motivation (screenshot 07)
Two camera modes (cockpit and chase) are both well-framed and toggle cleanly; chase cam (screenshots 05-06) reads kart direction and track ahead well and is a meaningful addition for desktop players
HUD is clean and unobtrusive: LAP, TIME, BEST, DELTA, and KM/H are all present in a single dark pill that does not obscure the track, with KM/H highlighted in orange for quick glancing

Controls card on the idle screen (screenshots 01, 10) simultaneously addresses desktop WASD, restart, camera toggle, and VR trigger mapping in one compact panel—excellent onboarding for a dual-mode title

issues.problem: DELTA column reads '---.--' for all three laps (screenshots 02-08); the delta against best lap is never populated during the race, gutting the core time-trial feedback loop that motivates ghost chasing
issues.fix: Compute sector or per-frame delta vs. the stored best-lap ghost timestamps and display '+0.00' / '-0.00' with red/green colouring from the moment lap 2 begins; ensure the value resets to 0.00 at each lap crossing rather than staying blank

issues.problem: Sense of speed in cockpit view is very low; screenshots 03-04 at 41-62 km/h feel static—no FOV pulse, no camera shake, no road blur, and the horizon barely moves despite the kart doing 82 km/h max (telemetry)
issues.fix: Add a subtle dynamic FOV increase (e.g. 70°→80° mapped to 0-82 km/h), a very slight high-frequency vertical camera bob tied to speed, and optionally a speed-lines vignette at the screen edge above 70 km/h to sell velocity in the seated cockpit perspective

issues.problem: Zero impact feedback: telemetry shows 0 impact samples and the traffic-cone interaction advertised in the brief produces no camera jolt, sound cue, or screen flash visible in any screenshot; hitting barriers also appears silent and consequence-free
issues.fix: On cone or barrier collision above a threshold impulse, trigger a 150ms camera shake (random offset ±0.03 m), a brief red vignette flash, and a short bump sound; for barrier contacts add a small velocity damping so the player feels the wall

issues.problem: Track layout appears to be almost entirely wide straights and gentle symmetric bends (screenshots 03-06 show identical barrier-lined corridors); there is no visible hairpin, chicane, or mixed-radius section to create pacing variety or a memorable racing line challenge
issues.fix: Introduce at least one tight hairpin (requiring genuine braking) and one double-apex or chicane sequence so lap rhythm alternates between full-throttle and technical sections; even at this scope a single hairpin raises replayability significantly

issues.problem: No off-track detection or consequence: the wide flat run-off areas visible in screenshots 05-06 mean a player can cut corners or go off-track with no speed penalty, warning message, or position reset, removing a layer of challenge and track-limit strategy
issues.fix: Detect when the kart centre leaves the tarmac polygon, immediately apply a 30-40% speed cap and display a brief 'Off track' warning on the HUD; optionally revert the lap time for that sector if a shortcut is detected

issues.problem: The 'Race complete' screen (screenshots 08-09) has a 'Press R or Restart' prompt but no visible on-screen Restart button for VR users who cannot press R on a keyboard; the in-race UI also lacks a minimap so players cannot preview upcoming corners
issues.fix: Add a world-space 'Restart' button or controller-ray-interactable panel visible in VR at the finish screen; add a small corner-dot minimap overlay (even a static SVG path) to the HUD so players can anticipate the next turn type
